content: The content provided appears to be a list of references from various studies, articles, and reviews related to health, infectious diseases, housing conditions, and other public health topics. 1. A study by Boshuizen et al. (2013) investigated the seasonal peaks in clustered and unique extra-pulmonary tuberculosis notifications, ruling out the winter crowding hypothesis. The findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis & Lung Disease. 2. Wingfield et al. (2014) explored the seasonality of tuberculosis in relation to sunlight, vitamin D levels, and household crowding. This research was detailed in the Journal of Infectious Diseases. 3. Yasar et al. (2011) reported a case of tuberculous meningoencephalitis with severe neurological sequelae in an immigrant child, as published in the Journal of Neurosciences in Rural Practice. 4. Zaman et al. (2014) conducted an epidemiological study on newly diagnosed sputum-positive tuberculosis patients in Dhubri district, Assam, India, focusing on factors influencing treatment compliance. The study appeared in the Journal of Natural Science, Biology & Medicine. 5. Zammarchi et al. (2014) reviewed tuberculosis in tropical areas and among immigrants, with findings published in the Mediterranean Journal of Hematology & Infectious Diseases. 6. Siddiqui et al. (2010) analyzed the investment in pediatric tuberculosis prevention in Pakistan, discussing whether it represents a loss or gain. The study was published in the Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association. 7. Adamia et al. (2012) examined the prevalence of bronchitis and associated risk factors in children, as reported in the World Allergy Organization Journal. 8. Mitra (2013) conducted a community-based prospective study in rural Bangladesh to identify risk factors and care-seeking behaviors for neonatal infections. This research was summarized in Dissertation Abstracts International. 9. Akintola and Hangulu (2014) explored infection control practices in home-based care for individuals living with HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis in South Africa. The findings were published in Global Public Health. 10. Banerji et al. (2009) identified risk factors and viruses associated with hospitalizations due to lower respiratory tract infections in Canadian Inuit children. The study was published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal. 11. Basta et al. (2012) provided age-specific prevalence estimates and risk factors for asymptomatic Neisseria meningitidis carriage in Bamako, Mali, as detailed in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 12. Bourrous et al. (2010) investigated the seroprevalence of viral hepatitis A in febrile icteric children in Marrakech, Morocco, with findings published in the Journal de Pédiatrie et de Puériculture. 13. Del Castillo-Sanchez et al. (2006) examined community-acquired pneumonia, focusing on risk factors and family functionality. The study was published in the Revista Medica del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social. 14. Braubach et al. (2011) quantified the health impacts of inadequate housing in the WHO European region, as part of a systematic review for the WHO Housing and Health Guidelines. 15. Charania and Tsuji (2011) assessed the response to the 2009 H1N1 pandemic in remote First Nation communities in Ontario, identifying barriers and improvements in healthcare services. The study was published in the International Journal of Circumpolar Health. 16. Chisti et al.
